items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: It is tempting to measure a city's generosity by the number of benches, fountains, and parks it builds. But a bench placed where no one passes is a monument, not an amenity. Urban designers increasingly argue that public space succeeds not when it is filled with objects but when it is _______: when people can linger, watch others, move a chair into the sun, or simply cut through on the way somewhere else. The best plazas are less like finished sculptures than like stages whose meaning depends on who shows up.
o: open to unplanned uses by the people who occupy it
designed to discourage people from staying long
protected from changes in the surrounding city
decorated with as many artworks as possible
reserved for official events and ceremonies
items.x: 공공장소는 사물로 채워질 때가 아니라 사람들이 자유롭게 머물고 쓰는 '계획되지 않은 사용'에 열려 있을 때 성공한다.

items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p:
Bees communicate the location of food through a 'waggle dance' performed inside the dark hive.
(A) Because the hive is dark, however, the other bees cannot watch the dance. Instead, they follow the dancer closely, sensing her movements through touch and vibration.
(B) The direction of the straight 'waggle run' indicates the direction of the food relative to the sun, while the length of the run signals the distance.
(C) In this way, information that was originally visual — the angle of the sun — is translated into a code that is received entirely without sight.
items.x: 춤의 의미(B) → 하지만 어두워서 촉각으로 감지(A, however) → 이렇게 시각 정보가 비시각 코드로(C, In this way).

items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p:
Economists distinguish between goods whose value falls as more people use them and goods whose value rises.
(A) A telephone network is the classic example of the second kind. A single telephone is worthless; its value grows with every new person who can be called.
(B) A crowded beach belongs to the first category: each additional visitor makes the experience slightly worse for everyone else.
(C) This difference explains why markets for the second kind tend toward a single dominant platform, while the first kind naturally spreads demand across many competitors.
items.x: 첫 번째 종류(B: first category) → 두 번째 종류(A: second kind) → 이 차이가 시장 구조를 설명(C).

items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p:
Early sailors had no reliable way to determine their longitude at sea.
(A) The solution, then, was not astronomical but mechanical: a clock that kept accurate time despite the rolling of a ship and changes in temperature.
(B) In principle, the problem was simple. Since the Earth rotates fifteen degrees every hour, comparing local noon with the time at a home port would reveal how far east or west a ship had traveled.
(C) The difficulty lay in knowing the time at the home port. Pendulum clocks, accurate on land, became hopelessly unreliable on a pitching deck.
items.x: 원리상 간단(B) → 어려움은 항구 시간 파악(C) → 따라서 해결책은 기계식 시계(A, then).

items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] Yet this apparent waste is precisely what allows the system to survive.
items.p: A forest that has not burned for a century may look healthy, crowded with tall trees and thick undergrowth. ( ① ) In reality, it is often more fragile than a forest that burns regularly. ( ② ) Small, frequent fires clear away dead material and young trees, destroying resources that could otherwise have grown. ( ③ ) Without them, fuel accumulates until a single spark produces a fire so intense that it kills even the oldest trees. ( ④ ) Forest managers have therefore begun to set controlled fires deliberately. ( ⑤ )
items.x: ③ 앞: 작은 불이 자원을 '파괴'(waste) → 주어진 문장(그러나 그 낭비가 생존을 가능케 함) → ③ 뒤: 불이 없으면 연료 축적.

items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] The reason is that the brain treats a broken streak as a loss.
items.p: Many apps reward users for practicing every day by displaying a 'streak' counter. ( ① ) At first, the counter simply provides encouragement. ( ② ) Over time, however, users report practicing not because they want to learn but because they cannot bear to see the number reset to zero. ( ③ ) Losses feel roughly twice as painful as equivalent gains feel pleasant, so protecting a 200-day streak can become more motivating than the skill itself. ( ④ ) Designers must decide whether this is a helpful nudge or a subtle trap. ( ⑤ )
items.x: ③ 앞: 숫자가 0이 되는 걸 못 견딤 → 주어진 문장(뇌는 끊긴 기록을 손실로 처리) → ③ 뒤: 손실이 이득보다 두 배 고통스럽다는 부연.

items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] On paper, waiting times dropped sharply; in reality, patients waited just as long.
items.p: Hospitals were once judged by how long patients waited in emergency rooms. ( ① ) The goal was sensible: shorter waits usually mean better care. ( ② ) But once administrators were rewarded for meeting the target, some began moving patients into hallways labeled 'assessment areas' to stop the clock. ( ③ ) A number that once reflected quality had become something to be managed for its own sake. ( ④ ) Economists summarize this pattern in a simple warning: when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. ( ⑤ )
items.x: ③: 복도로 옮겨 시계를 멈춘 조치(원인) 직후, 서류상 대기시간 감소·실제는 동일(결과)이 와야 '숫자가 그 자체로 관리 대상이 됐다'는 해석으로 이어진다.

items.q: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
items.p: Octopuses are remarkable problem solvers. ① In laboratories they have learned to unscrew jar lids to reach food inside. ② Some have escaped their tanks at night, crossed the floor, and raided neighboring tanks before returning. ③ Unlike vertebrates, most of an octopus's neurons are located in its arms rather than its central brain. ④ Octopuses are also a popular dish in many coastal cuisines, often grilled or served raw. ⑤ This distributed nervous system may allow each arm to explore and solve problems semi-independently.
items.x: 문어의 문제 해결 능력과 신경계에 관한 글 → ④ 요리 재료로서의 문어는 무관.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
[요약] People judge risks less by their actual ___(A)___ than by how easily examples come to mind, which is shaped largely by ___(B)___.
items.p: After a plane crash receives heavy news coverage, many travelers switch to driving, even though driving the same distance is far more dangerous. Shark attacks, which kill only a handful of people each year, generate more fear than heart disease, which kills millions. The pattern is consistent: dramatic, vivid events that are easy to picture loom larger in our minds than common, quiet threats. Since the news reports what is unusual rather than what is typical, our sense of danger is constantly pulled away from the statistics.
items.x: 실제 빈도(통계)보다 떠올리기 쉬움으로 위험을 판단하며, 이는 언론 보도가 좌우한다.

items.q: 밑줄 친 'the scaffolding was taken for the building'이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: For centuries, students learned geometry by memorizing Euclid's proofs line by line. The proofs were meant to be a means of training the mind to reason from assumptions to conclusions. Over time, however, recitation became the goal itself: a student who could repeat a proof flawlessly was considered to have mastered geometry, even if he could not prove a single new statement. In effect, the scaffolding was taken for the building.
o: A tool for developing a skill was mistaken for the skill itself.
Geometry was replaced by more practical subjects.
Students preferred building models to writing proofs.
Teachers abandoned Euclid for modern textbooks.
Memorization proved more useful than reasoning.
items.x: 비계(수단)를 건물(목적)로 착각 → 추론력을 기르는 수단인 증명 암기를 실력 자체로 오인.

items.q: 밑줄 친 'paying rent on an empty room'이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Many of us hold on to commitments long after they have stopped giving us anything: a club we no longer enjoy, a subscription we never use, a grudge against someone we barely remember. Each requires a small, steady payment of time, money, or emotional energy. Keeping them is like paying rent on an empty room.
o: continuing to invest in something that no longer serves us
sharing resources with people in need
moving to a smaller and cheaper place
forgetting obligations we have promised to keep
items.x: 더 이상 아무것도 주지 않는 것에 계속 비용을 지불하는 것.

items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.p: The researchers, ①whose findings were published last month, argued that the decline in bird populations ②is linked to changes in insect numbers. Species that rely heavily on insects during the breeding season ③have suffered most. Surprisingly, birds that feed on seeds ④remaining relatively stable, ⑤suggesting that food supply is a key factor.
items.x: birds that feed on seeds가 주어이고 본동사가 필요 → remaining → have remained / remained.

items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.p: Not until the invention of the microscope ①did scientists realize that a drop of pond water contains thousands of living organisms. Before then, life was assumed to exist only at scales ②visible to the naked eye. The discovery forced naturalists to reconsider ③what counted as an organism and ④how such tiny creatures reproduced. It was this shift in perspective ⑤what eventually led to the germ theory of disease.
items.x: It is ~ that 강조구문 → what을 that으로. ① Not until 도치 정상, ② 형용사 후치수식, ③④ 간접의문/명사절 정상.

items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.p: Having ①been warned about the storm, the hikers decided to turn back. The trail, ②which had been easy that morning, was now covered with mud so deep ③that each step required effort. By the time they reached the parking lot, two of them ④had lost their shoes, and all of them were ⑤exhausting.
items.x: 사람이 지친 상태 → exhausted. exhausting은 '지치게 하는'.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 옳은 문장은?
o: Hardly had she arrived when the meeting started.
Neither the coach nor the players was aware of the change.
The number of students who applies has doubled.
He suggested that she goes to the doctor at once.
It is the first time that I visit this museum.
items.x: Hardly had p.p. ~ when 과거 도치 정상. ② 가까운 주어 players → were, ③ who 선행사 students → apply, ④ suggest(제안) that S (should) go, ⑤ It is the first time 현재완료 have visited.

items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.p: Before refrigeration, preserving food was a constant ①challenge. Salting, smoking, and drying all worked by ②removing the moisture that bacteria need to grow. These methods, though effective, often ③altered the taste and texture of food. The refrigerator changed this by slowing bacterial growth without ④transforming the food itself, allowing fresh produce to travel long distances. As a result, diets became far more ⑤uniform, as people gained access to fruits and vegetables from distant regions and different seasons.
items.x: 먼 지역·다른 계절의 식품에 접근 → 식단이 '다양해졌다'(varied/diverse). uniform(획일적인)은 부적절.

items.q: (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Good scientists are (A)[skeptical / credulous] of results that seem too neat. When an experiment confirms a hypothesis perfectly, they look for hidden errors before (B)[celebrating / dismissing] the finding. This habit may seem pessimistic, but it (C)[undermines / strengthens] the reliability of science over time.
items.x: 너무 깔끔한 결과를 의심(skeptical) → 축하하기 전에 오류 확인(celebrating) → 신뢰성을 강화(strengthens).

items.q: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: When a translator renders a poem from one language into another, she faces an impossible choice. If she preserves the literal meaning, the rhythm and rhyme are lost. If she recreates the music, she must invent words the poet never wrote. Every translation, therefore, is also an interpretation: a decision about which qualities of the original matter most. Readers who believe they are reading the poet's words are, in part, reading the translator's judgment.
o: the unavoidable role of interpretation in translation
the superiority of literal translation over free translation
the history of translating poetry into English
why poems should never be translated
the difficulty of learning a second language
items.x: 번역은 무엇을 살릴지 선택하는 해석 행위일 수밖에 없다.

items.q: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: We often praise children for being 'smart' when they succeed. The intention is kind, but the message can backfire. A child told that success reflects a fixed trait learns that failure must reflect the absence of that trait. Faced with a harder problem, such a child may avoid it altogether rather than risk evidence that she is not smart after all. Praise directed at effort and strategy, by contrast, frames difficulty as part of the process rather than a verdict on ability.
o: 능력보다 노력과 전략을 칭찬해야 도전을 피하지 않는다.
실패 경험은 가능한 한 줄여 주어야 한다.
items.x: '똑똑하다'는 칭찬은 고정된 능력관을 심어 도전을 회피하게 한다 → 노력·전략 칭찬.

items.q: As used in the passage, 'arrested' most nearly means:
items.p: The sudden collapse of the bridge arrested all traffic between the two towns for nearly a month, forcing merchants to find longer routes through the mountains.
items.x: 교통을 '멈추게 했다' → halted.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word?
items.p: Although the novelist was famously ______ in interviews, offering only one-word answers, her letters to friends reveal a witty and expansive personality.
items.x: 한 단어 대답 → 말수가 적은(taciturn). Although로 대조되는 편지 속 수다스러운 성격.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word?
items.p: The committee's report was criticized as ______: it acknowledged the problem in general terms but offered no specific recommendations that could be implemented or evaluated.
items.x: 구체적 제안 없이 무난하기만 함 → anodyne(무난한, 밋밋한).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.p: Researchers expected the new fertilizer to increase crop yields in dry regions. ______, yields fell slightly, apparently because the fertilizer increased the plants' need for water.
items.x: 기대(증가)와 반대 결과(감소) → Instead.

items.q: Which choice most logically completes the text?
items.p: In a study of 40 lakes, ecologists found that lakes with more species of algae recovered faster after pollution events than lakes with fewer species. However, in lakes where one algae species made up more than 80% of the total, the number of species had no effect on recovery time. This suggests that ______
o: the benefit of species diversity depends on no single species being overwhelmingly dominant.
pollution affects only lakes with many algae species.
dominant algae species cause pollution events.
recovery time is unrelated to the number of algae species in any lake.
ecologists should remove dominant species from all lakes.
items.x: 종 다양성의 효과는 한 종이 압도적으로 우세하지 않을 때만 나타난다.

items.q: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: In the 1950s, engineers designing cockpits for the U.S. Air Force measured thousands of pilots and built seats to fit the 'average' pilot. Accidents remained high. When one researcher checked how many pilots actually fell within the average range on ten key body dimensions, the answer was zero. A cockpit designed for the average fit no one. The solution was adjustable seats, pedals, and helmet straps — features we now take for granted in every car. The lesson extends beyond aviation: systems designed around an imaginary average person often fail the real individuals they are meant to serve.
o: Designing for Everyone by Designing for No One in Particular
Why Pilots Need Better Training Programs
The Rising Cost of Military Aircraft
How Cars Borrowed Ideas from Airplanes
Statistics as the Key to Safer Flights
items.x: '평균'에 맞춘 설계는 아무에게도 맞지 않음 → 조절 가능하게(특정 누구도 아닌 모두를 위해) 설계해야 함.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: A musician who practices a piece only at full speed tends to rehearse her mistakes along with the notes. Slowing down feels like going backward, yet it is precisely at slow tempos that errors become visible and can be corrected before they are absorbed into muscle memory. Speed, in this view, is not something one practices directly; it is _______.
o: the by-product of accuracy repeated until it becomes effortless
a natural talent that cannot be developed
the first goal every beginner should set
less important than the choice of instrument
a skill that declines with careful practice
items.x: 속도는 직접 연습하는 것이 아니라 정확성을 반복한 결과로 생긴다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Early automobiles were called 'horseless carriages,' and their designers placed the driver high and in front, exactly where a coachman would sit. New technologies are often first understood through the forms of the old ones they replace. Only gradually do designers realize that the new tool has _______, and the familiar shape gives way to something genuinely new.
o: possibilities the old form was never built to express
the same limitations as the horse
no practical use for ordinary people
items.x: 새 기술은 처음엔 옛 형태로 이해되다가 옛 형태가 담을 수 없는 가능성을 지녔음을 깨닫게 된다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: When researchers asked people to predict how happy they would be a year after winning the lottery or after a serious setback, most expected dramatic and lasting changes. In reality, both groups returned surprisingly close to their earlier levels of well-being. Humans, it seems, are poor forecasters of their own emotions because they _______.
o: underestimate how quickly they adapt to new circumstances
remember past events with perfect accuracy
care little about money or health
prefer stability to any kind of change
items.x: 쾌락 적응: 사람들은 새로운 상황에 얼마나 빨리 적응하는지를 과소평가한다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: A good editor rarely adds much to a manuscript. Most of the work consists of cutting: removing the paragraph the author loves but the reader does not need, the clever phrase that draws attention to itself. The finished book is often stronger not because of what the editor contributed but because of _______.
o: what the editor persuaded the author to give up
how many new chapters were written
the fame of the publishing company
the number of pages in the final version
the author's refusal to accept advice
items.x: 편집의 핵심은 삭제 → 편집자가 작가에게 포기하게 한 것 덕분에 강해진다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: In many ant colonies, no single ant knows where food is or how the nest should be built. Each follows simple rules: lay a scent trail when carrying food, follow stronger trails more often. From thousands of such local decisions, efficient paths and complex structures emerge. The intelligence of the colony, therefore, resides _______.
o: in the interactions among individuals rather than in any one of them
in the queen, who directs every worker
in the largest and oldest ants
in the genes of a few special scouts
outside the colony, in the environment alone
items.x: 창발: 집단 지능은 개체 간 상호 작용에 있다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: We often treat boredom as a problem to be solved immediately with a phone or a screen. Yet psychologists suggest that boredom serves a function: it signals that our current activity no longer satisfies us and pushes us to seek something more meaningful. Constantly escaping boredom may therefore _______.
o: silence a signal that could lead us toward better goals
make us more creative than ever before
help us concentrate on difficult tasks
reduce the time we spend on screens
prove that boredom has no purpose
items.x: 지루함은 더 의미 있는 것을 찾게 하는 신호 → 피하기만 하면 그 신호를 꺼 버린다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Translators of legal documents face a problem that literary translators rarely do: a term may have no equivalent in the target legal system. 'Trust' in English law, for instance, describes an arrangement that some civil-law countries simply do not recognize. Translating the word is easy; translating the concept requires _______.
o: explaining an entire framework that the reader's system lacks
ignoring the differences between legal systems
items.x: 법률 용어는 개념 자체가 없는 경우가 있어 그 체계 전체를 설명해야 한다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Athletes who visualize a performance in detail — the feel of the ball, the sound of the crowd, the exact movement of each muscle — often improve more than those who merely practice physically. Brain scans show that imagining an action activates many of the same regions as performing it. For the brain, a vividly imagined rehearsal is _______.
items.x: 생생한 상상 리허설은 뇌에게 부분적으로 실제 연습이다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Historians caution against judging past societies by whether they 'anticipated' the present. A medieval physician who failed to discover germs was not foolish; he reasoned carefully from the evidence available to him. To read history only as a march toward our own beliefs is to _______.
o: mistake our position in time for superior intelligence
understand the past exactly as it was
give proper credit to medieval science
items.x: 현재를 기준으로 과거를 재단하는 것은 시간상의 위치를 지적 우월성으로 착각하는 것.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Cities that build more roads to reduce traffic often find that congestion soon returns to its former level. New lanes make driving more attractive, so people who previously took the bus, traveled at other times, or stayed home begin to drive. In this way, increasing road capacity can _______.
o: generate the very demand it was meant to relieve
reduce the number of cars on the road
encourage people to use public transport
lower the cost of building new roads
items.x: 유발 수요: 도로 확충이 해소하려던 수요를 스스로 만들어 낸다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Mistakes in a second language are often treated as failures, but many linguists see them as evidence of learning. A child who says 'I goed to school' has not simply copied an error; she has discovered the rule for forming the past tense and applied it too widely. Her mistake reveals _______.
o: an underlying system being actively constructed
a complete lack of grammatical knowledge
that rules are unnecessary in language
a memory problem that needs treatment
items.x: 과잉 일반화 오류는 규칙 체계를 능동적으로 구성하고 있다는 증거.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Many inventions that changed the world were not the work of a lone genius but appeared almost simultaneously in different places. The telephone, calculus, and the theory of evolution each had more than one independent discoverer. This pattern suggests that discoveries depend less on individual brilliance than on _______.
o: the readiness of the surrounding knowledge and tools
luck that strikes only once in history
government orders to invent specific things
items.x: 동시 발견: 발견은 주변 지식과 도구가 무르익었는지에 달려 있다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: When a restaurant menu lists a very expensive dish at the top, few customers order it. Its real purpose is to make the second-most-expensive dish look reasonable by comparison. Our judgments of value are rarely absolute; they are _______.
o: shaped by whatever reference points happen to surround them
fixed by the actual cost of ingredients
independent of how options are presented
always correct when we are hungry
items.x: 앵커링/대비 효과: 가치 판단은 주변 기준점에 의해 형성된다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: A scientist who reports only the experiments that worked gives a distorted picture of nature. Failed experiments also contain information: they tell others which paths are not worth taking. When journals publish only positive results, the entire field _______.
o: risks repeating mistakes that were never made public
has no need for further research
items.x: 출판 편향: 실패 결과가 공개되지 않으면 같은 실수를 반복할 위험이 있다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Some forests appear peaceful, but beneath the soil, trees compete intensely for water and nutrients. Yet the same underground fungal networks that carry this competition also transfer sugars from large trees to shaded seedlings. The forest is thus neither purely a battlefield nor purely a community; it is _______.
o: a system in which rivalry and cooperation are woven together
a place where only the strongest trees survive
a peaceful home with no competition
items.x: 숲은 경쟁과 협력이 함께 엮인 체계.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Students who reread their notes several times often feel confident, because the material looks increasingly familiar. But familiarity is not the same as memory. When tested, those who instead tried to recall the material without looking usually perform far better. The feeling of fluency, in other words, can be _______.
o: a misleading indicator of how much we have learned
the most reliable sign of mastery
a result of testing ourselves too often
items.x: 유창성 착각: 친숙함은 학습량의 오해를 부르는 지표.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Maps of the medieval world often placed Jerusalem at the center and filled distant regions with imaginary creatures. To modern eyes these maps look inaccurate, but they were never meant to guide travelers. They expressed how their makers understood the world's meaning and order. Judged by their purpose, they were _______.
o: accurate representations of a worldview rather than of geography
useless documents made by careless artists
copies of older and more precise maps
items.x: 중세 지도는 지리가 아니라 세계관을 정확히 표현한 것.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Negotiators often say that the person who cares least about the outcome holds the most power. If you are willing to walk away, the other side must offer more to keep you at the table. Preparing a good alternative before negotiating is therefore valuable not because you will use it, but because _______.
o: it changes how much you need the deal in front of you
it guarantees the other side will accept your terms
it allows you to avoid negotiating entirely
it proves you are more honest
items.x: 대안(BATNA)은 현재 거래에 대한 의존도를 바꿔 협상력을 높인다.

items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p:
Salt was once so valuable that it was used as a form of payment.
(A) This need for salt shaped trade routes across deserts and seas, and cities grew wealthy by controlling its supply.
(B) Before refrigeration, it was one of the few reliable ways to preserve meat and fish through long winters.
(C) Today, cheap and abundant, salt has lost that importance, which is perhaps why we forget how much history it once directed.
items.x: 가치의 이유(B: 보존) → 그 필요가 무역로를 형성(A: This need) → 오늘날(C).

items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p:
A placebo is a treatment with no active ingredient, yet patients who receive one often report real improvement.
(A) Even more surprisingly, the effect can persist when patients are told openly that the pill contains nothing.
(B) Researchers once attributed this simply to patients' desire to please their doctors.
(C) Later studies, however, found measurable changes in the brain, including the release of natural pain-relieving chemicals.
items.x: 초기 설명(B) → 그러나 뇌 변화 발견(C, however) → 더 놀랍게도 공개해도 효과 지속(A, Even more).

items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p:
In the nineteenth century, many doctors refused to believe that washing their hands could save lives.
(A) When he required doctors in his ward to wash with a chlorine solution, deaths dropped sharply.
(B) One physician, Ignaz Semmelweis, noticed that mothers in a ward run by doctors died far more often than those in a ward run by midwives.
(C) Yet because he could not explain why it worked, his colleagues dismissed his findings for decades.
items.x: 관찰(B) → 손 씻기 도입·사망률 감소(A, he) → 그러나 무시됨(C, Yet).

items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p:
Economists use the term 'tragedy of the commons' to describe what happens when a shared resource is open to everyone.
(A) The result is that the resource is overused until it collapses, harming every user, including those who caused the damage.
(B) Each herder, for example, gains the full benefit of adding one more animal to a shared pasture, while the cost of overgrazing is spread among all.
(C) Solutions range from private ownership to community rules, but all aim to make individuals bear more of the costs they create.
items.x: 예시(B) → 결과(A) → 해결책(C).

items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p:
The first photographs required subjects to sit perfectly still for several minutes.
(A) That is why people in early portraits rarely smile: holding a smile for so long was nearly impossible.
(B) Over time, faster chemical processes reduced exposure times to fractions of a second.
(C) Only then did candid images of laughter and movement become possible, changing how people presented themselves to the camera.
items.x: 결과(A: 웃지 않음) → 노출 시간 단축(B) → 그제야 자연스러운 사진(C, Only then).

items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p:
Most people assume that a stronger password must be harder to remember.
(A) A phrase such as 'purple tiger drinks cold coffee' is both easier to recall and harder for a computer to guess.
(B) In fact, length matters far more than complexity, because each additional character multiplies the number of possible combinations.
(C) Security experts therefore recommend long, memorable phrases over short strings of random symbols.
items.x: 반박(B: In fact) → 예시(A) → 결론(C: therefore).

items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] This, however, is not a sign of laziness.
items.p: Teenagers often stay up late and struggle to wake up in the morning. ( ① ) Parents and teachers frequently interpret this as a lack of discipline. ( ② ) During adolescence, the body's internal clock shifts, releasing the sleep hormone melatonin later at night. ( ③ ) As a result, a teenager who goes to bed at ten may simply be unable to fall asleep. ( ④ ) Some schools have responded by starting classes later, with improvements in attendance and grades. ( ⑤ )
items.x: 게으름으로 해석(②앞) → 그러나 게으름의 신호가 아님 → 생체 시계 변화 설명.

items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] The trick works only because the audience never thinks to look there.
items.p: Magicians rarely rely on speed to deceive their audiences. ( ① ) Instead, they control where attention goes. ( ② ) A dramatic gesture with the right hand draws every eye, while the left hand quietly performs the secret move in plain view. ( ③ ) Neuroscientists have become interested in such techniques because they reveal the limits of human perception. ( ④ ) We see far less than we believe we see, and what we notice is shaped by what we expect. ( ⑤ )
items.x: 왼손이 '눈앞에서' 비밀 동작 → 관객이 그곳을 볼 생각을 안 하기 때문에 통한다 → 신경과학자의 관심.

items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] Within weeks, the rats had multiplied far beyond anyone's control.
items.p: In the early twentieth century, colonial officials in Hanoi offered a reward for every rat killed. ( ① ) To prove their work, hunters only had to bring in the rats' tails. ( ② ) Soon officials noticed tailless rats running through the city. ( ③ ) Hunters had been cutting off tails and releasing the animals to breed more rewards, and some even began farming rats. ( ④ ) The policy, intended to reduce the population, had made the problem worse. ( ⑤ )
items.x: 쥐를 사육하기까지 함(④ 앞) → 몇 주 만에 통제 불능으로 번식 → 정책이 문제를 악화시켰다는 결론.

items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] In other words, the river had been carrying the land to the sea.
items.p: For centuries, farmers along the Nile depended on its annual flood. ( ① ) The water spread rich silt across the fields, renewing the soil every year. ( ② ) After a large dam was built upstream, the floods stopped and the silt remained trapped behind the wall. ( ③ ) Farmers had to buy chemical fertilizers, and the delta at the river's mouth began to shrink. ( ④ ) Without fresh sediment, the coastline was slowly eaten away by waves. ( ⑤ )
items.x: 삼각주가 퇴적물 없이 깎여 나감(⑤ 앞) → 다시 말해 강은 땅을 바다로 실어 날라 삼각주를 유지해 왔다는 정리.

items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
[주어진 문장] Yet the number of words a child hears is only part of the story.
items.p: Studies have found that children from homes with frequent conversation develop larger vocabularies. ( ① ) This led many programs to encourage parents simply to talk more. ( ② ) Later research showed that back-and-forth exchanges, in which the child responds and the adult answers, matter more than one-way speech. ( ③ ) A child listening to a television for hours learns little compared with one who is engaged in conversation. ( ④ ) Quality of interaction, not just quantity, shapes language growth. ( ⑤ )
items.x: 말을 많이 하라고 권장(②앞) → 그러나 단어 수는 일부일 뿐 → 주고받는 대화가 더 중요.

items.q: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
items.p: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they support about a quarter of all marine species. ① They provide shelter, breeding grounds, and food for thousands of organisms. ② Reefs also protect coastlines by absorbing the energy of waves during storms. ③ Some reef fish change color at night to avoid predators. ④ Rising ocean temperatures, however, cause corals to expel the algae they depend on, a process known as bleaching. ⑤ If bleaching continues, the many species and coastal communities that rely on reefs will face serious losses.
items.x: 산호초의 가치와 백화 위협에 관한 글 → ③ 물고기의 야간 체색 변화는 무관.

items.q: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
items.p: Many companies now allow employees to work from home several days a week. ① Supporters argue that remote work saves commuting time and increases concentration. ② Critics respond that spontaneous conversations, which often spark new ideas, happen less often online. ③ Some studies suggest that new employees, in particular, learn more slowly without colleagues nearby. ④ The first personal computers were sold to the public in the late 1970s. ⑤ As a result, many firms are experimenting with hybrid schedules that combine both arrangements.
items.x: 재택근무 찬반과 하이브리드 근무 → ④ 개인용 컴퓨터 판매 역사는 무관.

items.q: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
items.p: Sleep plays a crucial role in memory. ① During deep sleep, the brain replays the day's experiences and strengthens important connections. ② Students who sleep after studying recall more than those who stay awake for the same period. ③ Some animals, such as dolphins, sleep with one half of the brain at a time. ④ Pulling an all-nighter before an exam can therefore undermine the very learning it is meant to secure. ⑤ Protecting sleep may be one of the most effective study strategies available.
items.x: 수면과 기억/학습 → ③ 돌고래의 반구 수면은 흐름에서 벗어남.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
[요약] When rewards are offered for an activity people already ___(A)___, the rewards can ___(B)___ their motivation once removed.
items.p: In one experiment, children who loved drawing were divided into groups. Some were promised a certificate for drawing; others were not. Weeks later, when no rewards were offered, the children who had received certificates spent much less time drawing than the others. Being paid for something they did for pleasure seemed to turn play into work, and when the payment stopped, so did the interest.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
[요약] Groups make better estimates when members judge ___(A)___ than when they first ___(B)___ with each other.
items.p: When hundreds of people guess the weight of an ox, the average of their guesses is often remarkably close to the truth, closer than most individual experts. But this works only when each guess is made independently. If people discuss their estimates first, they tend to converge on the opinion of the most confident speaker, and the errors no longer cancel out.
items.x: 군중의 지혜는 독립적 판단에서 나온다. 먼저 논의하면 오차가 상쇄되지 않는다.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
[요약] Seeing many ___(A)___ examples can make people believe a risk is more ___(B)___ than it really is.
items.p: After watching several news stories about shark attacks, swimmers often become afraid to enter the ocean, even though the chance of being bitten is extremely small. Our minds estimate how common an event is by how easily we can recall examples of it. Vivid, recent stories come to mind quickly, so they distort our sense of probability.

items.q: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Bilingual speakers constantly manage two languages, suppressing one while using the other. This continuous control appears to exercise the brain's systems for attention and switching between tasks. Some studies have found that bilingual adults are better at ignoring distractions, and that lifelong bilingualism may even delay the symptoms of age-related memory decline.
o: cognitive benefits of managing two languages
difficulties children face in learning languages
why bilingual people forget their first language
how to choose a second language to study
items.x: 두 언어를 관리하는 것의 인지적 이점.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: When the first antibiotics were introduced, doctors believed infectious disease would soon be defeated. Within years, however, bacteria resistant to the new drugs appeared. Each time a drug is used, the few bacteria that happen to survive pass on their resistance. Overusing antibiotics, in animals as well as people, accelerates this process, turning a medical miracle into a race we may be losing.
o: The Hidden Arms Race Against Bacteria
Doctors Who Refuse to Prescribe Drugs
items.x: 항생제 남용 → 내성균 진화 → 우리가 지고 있을지 모르는 경쟁.

items.q: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Many people wait to feel motivated before starting a difficult task. But motivation often follows action rather than preceding it. Once you begin, even with a small step such as writing a single sentence, the task becomes less intimidating and momentum builds. Waiting for inspiration can mean waiting forever.

어려운 일은 처음부터 크게 시작해야 한다.

items.x: 동기는 행동에 앞서기보다 뒤따른다.

items.q: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: A city's sidewalks do more than move pedestrians. When shops face the street and people walk past at all hours, residents become informal watchers who notice strangers and trouble. Urban writer Jane Jacobs called this 'eyes on the street.' Neighborhoods designed around cars and empty plazas lose this natural surveillance and can feel less safe, even with more police.
o: the role of active street life in creating safety
the need for more police in modern cities
why cars are essential to urban life
the decline of shopping in city centers

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: The color of a plate can change how food tastes. In experiments, the same strawberry dessert was rated sweeter when served on a white plate than on a black one. Heavier cutlery made diners judge a meal as higher in quality, and background music affected whether a wine seemed fruity or bitter. Flavor, it turns out, is constructed by all the senses, not by the tongue alone.
o: Tasting with More Than the Tongue
How to Cook a Perfect Dessert

items.q: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: We tend to believe that our memories are faithful recordings of the past. Yet each time we recall an event, we reconstruct it, filling gaps with expectations and later information. Eyewitnesses who are confident are not necessarily accurate, and detailed false memories can be created through suggestion. Memory is less like a video file than like a story retold.

items.q: 밑줄 친 'fighting the last war'가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Military planners are often accused of 'fighting the last war': preparing for the kind of conflict that defeated them before, rather than the one that is coming. Businesses do the same when they defend against yesterday's competitors while a new technology quietly makes their entire product obsolete.

items.q: 밑줄 친 'a map, not the territory'가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: A company's financial report may show steady growth, yet employees may be exhausted and customers quietly leaving. Numbers simplify reality so that it can be managed. Leaders who forget this begin to manage the numbers instead of the business. A spreadsheet is a map, not the territory.

a document useful only for travelers
proof that a company is succeeding

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
items.p: In 1928, Alexander Fleming returned from vacation to find mold growing on one of his bacterial cultures. Around the mold, the bacteria had died. Rather than discarding the contaminated dish, he investigated and identified the substance responsible, which he named penicillin. Yet Fleming could not produce it in useful quantities, and the discovery attracted little attention for over a decade. It was only during the Second World War that a team at Oxford developed methods to purify and mass-produce the drug, saving countless lives.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 옳은 문장은?
o: Not only did he finish the project, but he also helped his teammates.
Not only he finished the project, but he also helped his teammates.
Not only did he finished the project, but he also helped his teammates.
Not only he did finish the project, but he also helped his teammates.
Not only finished he the project, but he also helped his teammates.
items.x: Not only 문두 → did he finish 도치.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
o: She made her son to clean his room.
She made her son clean his room.
She let her son play outside.
She had her son wash the car.
She got her son to clean his room.
items.x: 사역동사 make + 목적어 + 동사원형.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 옳은 문장은?
o: Whatever you decide, I will support you.
Whatever you will decide, I will support you will.
Whoever you decide, I will support it.
However you decide it what, I will support you.
Whatever do you decide, I will support you.
items.x: 복합관계사 whatever + S V (양보 부사절, 현재시제로 미래 표현).

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
o: The man who's car was stolen called the police.
The man whose car was stolen called the police.
The man who called the police lost his car.
The police found the car that was stolen.
The car, which was stolen, was found.
items.x: 소유격 관계대명사 whose (who's = who is).

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 옳은 문장은?
o: So difficult was the exam that few students passed.
So difficult the exam was that few students passed it was.
So the exam was difficult that few students passed.
So difficult was the exam which few students passed.
Such difficult was the exam that few students passed.
items.x: So + 형용사 + V + S + that 도치 구문.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
o: I have seen that movie last year.
I saw that movie last year.
I have seen that movie twice.
I had seen that movie before I read the book.
I have never seen such a movie.
items.x: 명백한 과거 시점(last year)과 현재완료 함께 불가.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 옳은 문장은?
o: Should you need any help, please contact me.
Should you needed any help, please contact me.
Should need you any help, please contact me.
If should you need any help, please contact me.
You should need any help, please contact me if.
items.x: If you should need → Should you need (if 생략 도치).

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
o: The committee are consisted of ten members.
The committee consists of ten members.
The committee is composed of ten members.
The committee is made up of ten members.
Ten members make up the committee.
items.x: consist of는 자동사 → 수동태 불가.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The scientist's conclusions were ______, resting on a single small experiment that no other laboratory had been able to replicate.
items.x: 근거가 빈약 → tenuous(근거가 약한).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: Rather than presenting a single unified theory, the book offers a ______ of perspectives, drawing on history, biology, and economics to examine the same question.
items.x: 여러 관점을 모은 것 → mosaic.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: Although critics initially dismissed the painter's work as ______, later generations recognized the careful technique beneath its apparent simplicity.
items.x: 단순해 보여 '순진한/소박한'으로 치부 → naive.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The negotiator's ______ manner — calm, patient, and never visibly frustrated — helped ease tensions between the two delegations.
items.x: 차분하고 인내심 있는 → equanimous(평정한).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The new policy had the ______ effect of increasing pollution: by lowering the price of fuel, it encouraged people to drive more.
items.x: 의도하지 않은 결과 → unintended.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: Far from being ______, the author's footnotes are essential to the argument, supplying evidence for nearly every major claim.
items.x: Far from ~ (전혀 ~가 아니라) essential → 반대말 superfluous(불필요한).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: Despite her ______ reputation as a harsh critic, the reviewer praised the young novelist's debut with unusual warmth.
items.x: 가혹한 비평가로서의 대단한/무서운 명성 → formidable.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: Historians have long debated whether the treaty ______ the war or merely delayed it; documents released recently suggest the latter.
items.x: 전쟁을 '막았는지' 아니면 늦췄을 뿐인지 → averted.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The documentary's ______ approach — presenting interviews from all sides without commentary — left viewers to draw their own conclusions.
items.x: 모든 쪽 인터뷰, 논평 없음 → impartial(공정한).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: Because the manuscript survives only in ______ form, with many pages missing or damaged, scholars must reconstruct parts of the text from later copies.
items.x: 페이지 누락·손상 → fragmentary(단편적인).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The mayor's promise to cut taxes while expanding every public service struck economists as ______, since the city's budget could not support both.
items.x: 예산상 둘 다 불가 → untenable(유지할 수 없는).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: Once considered a ______ concern of a few specialists, data privacy has become a central issue in public debate.
items.x: 소수 전문가의 '주변적' 관심 → 이제 중심 쟁점 → peripheral.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The biologist's notes were remarkably ______: every observation was dated, measured, and cross-referenced with earlier entries.
items.x: 모두 날짜·측정·교차 참조 → meticulous(꼼꼼한).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The poet's later work is marked by ______: where her early poems were long and ornate, the later ones use few words and almost no imagery.
items.x: 말수 적고 이미지 거의 없음 → austerity(간소함).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: Although the two species look nearly ______, genetic analysis shows they diverged millions of years ago.
items.x: Although 대조: 거의 똑같아 보이지만 유전적으로 오래전에 갈라짐 → identical.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The CEO's apology was widely viewed as ______: it expressed regret in general terms but admitted no specific wrongdoing and promised no changes.
items.x: 형식적인 사과 → perfunctory.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The engineer proposed a ______ solution: rather than replacing the entire bridge, crews would reinforce only the weakest supports.
items.x: 현실적·실용적 해법 → pragmatic.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: Scholars have found it difficult to ______ the philosopher's early and late writings, which seem to contradict each other on several key points.
items.x: 서로 모순되는 저작을 '조화시키기' 어렵다 → reconcile.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.p: Many desert plants store water in thick stems. ______, some species have roots that extend more than 20 meters underground to reach deep water sources.
items.x: 물 확보의 다른 전략 → Alternatively.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.p: The city spent millions on new bike lanes, expecting cycling to rise sharply. ______, the number of cyclists grew only slightly in the first year, though it increased steadily afterward.
items.x: 기대(급증)와 달리 첫해는 약간 → 대조 Initially, however.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.p: The museum extended its hours to attract more visitors. ______, attendance on weekday evenings nearly doubled.
items.x: 원인-결과 → As a result.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.p: Some historians credit the printing press with spreading scientific ideas. Others, ______, argue that existing networks of letters among scholars were just as important.
items.x: 다른 학자들은 대조적 주장 → by contrast.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.p: The novel was rejected by eleven publishers. ______, it went on to sell millions of copies and was translated into forty languages.
items.x: 거절에도 불구하고 성공 → Nonetheless.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.p: Octopuses can change both the color and the texture of their skin. ______, they can make their skin appear smooth like sand or bumpy like coral, depending on their surroundings.
items.x: 앞 내용의 구체화 → Specifically.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.p: The researchers expected the drug to lower blood pressure in all patients. ______, it had no measurable effect on patients over seventy.
items.x: 예상과 반대 → However.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.p: Early telescopes produced blurry images because different colors of light focused at different points. ______, astronomers began using curved mirrors instead of lenses, which reflect all colors equally.
items.x: 문제에 대한 해결 → To solve this problem.

items.q: Which choice most logically completes the text?
items.p: Researchers found that bees exposed to a common pesticide still visited flowers but returned to the hive with less pollen. Further tests showed that the bees' ability to learn which flowers were most rewarding was impaired. These findings suggest that the pesticide ______
o: harms colonies indirectly by reducing foraging efficiency rather than by killing bees outright.
has no effect on bee behavior.
improves bees' ability to find flowers.
items.x: 꽃은 방문하지만 효율 저하·학습 장애 → 간접적 피해.

items.q: Which choice most logically completes the text?
items.p: In a study of reading habits, participants who read on paper remembered the order of events in a story better than those who read the same story on a screen. Both groups, however, scored equally on questions about characters and setting. This suggests that reading on screens ______
o: may specifically affect memory for sequence rather than comprehension in general.
makes it impossible to understand characters.
has no effect on any kind of memory.
is better than reading on paper.
items.x: 순서 기억만 차이 → 순서 기억에 특정적으로 영향.

items.q: Which choice most logically completes the text?
items.p: Archaeologists discovered tools made of a stone that is found only in a region 300 kilometers away from the site. No evidence suggests the site's inhabitants traveled that far. The archaeologists therefore concluded that ______
o: the stone or tools likely arrived through trade with other groups.
the inhabitants never used stone tools.
the stone formed naturally at the site.
the tools were made after the site was abandoned.
items.x: 원거리 산지 + 이동 증거 없음 → 교역으로 유입.

items.q: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
items.p: For decades, the giant panda was classified as endangered. Conservation efforts, including habitat protection and breeding programs, increased the wild population by nearly 20 percent. In 2016, the species was reclassified as vulnerable, though experts warn that climate change could still threaten its bamboo forests.
o: Conservation has improved the panda's status, but future risks remain.
Giant pandas are no longer at any risk.
Breeding programs have failed to help pandas.
Climate change has already destroyed panda habitats.
items.x: 보전 노력으로 지위 개선, 그러나 위험 잔존.

items.q: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the researchers' claim?
items.p: Researchers claim that a new teaching method causes higher math scores, because students in schools using the method scored 15% higher than students in other schools.
o: The schools using the method also had much smaller class sizes than the other schools.
Students using the method enjoyed math more.
The method has been used for several years.
Teachers needed training to use the method.
The method was developed by a university.
items.x: 학급 규모라는 교란 변수 → 인과 주장 약화.

items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.p: Social media platforms are designed to ①capture attention for as long as possible. Notifications, endless scrolling, and unpredictable rewards ②encourage users to keep checking their phones. Over time, this can ③fragment concentration and make deep reading more difficult. Some users respond by ④limiting app use or turning off notifications, a strategy that has been shown to ⑤reduce their ability to focus.
items.x: 알림을 끄는 전략은 집중력을 '향상시킨다(improve)' → reduce 부적절.

items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.p: Vaccines work by ①training the immune system to recognize a specific threat. When a large share of the population is immune, a disease has difficulty ②spreading, which protects even those who cannot be vaccinated. This ③collective protection is known as herd immunity. If vaccination rates ④decline, however, outbreaks can return, as the pool of ⑤resistant individuals grows large enough to sustain transmission.
items.x: 전파를 유지시키는 것은 '감염되기 쉬운(susceptible)' 사람들의 집단 → resistant 부적절.

items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.p: Bamboo is one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth, with some species ①gaining nearly a meter in a single day. Because it ②regenerates quickly after harvesting, it is often promoted as a ③sustainable building material. Its strength is ④comparable to that of steel in tension, yet it is far ⑤heavier, making it easy to transport.
items.x: 운반하기 쉬운 이유 → 훨씬 '가볍다(lighter)'. heavier 부적절.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The startup's early success proved ______: within two years, competitors had copied its product and its sales collapsed.
items.x: 2년 만에 무너짐 → ephemeral(덧없는, 일시적인).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The historian warns against ______ the past, noting that the 'good old days' included widespread disease and poverty.
items.x: 좋았던 옛날을 미화하지 말라 → romanticizing.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: Her argument was so ______ that even critics who disagreed with her conclusions admired the clarity of her reasoning.
items.x: 명료한 추론 → cogent(설득력 있는).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: Because the rare orchid blooms for only one night each year, botanists who wish to study it must be ______ and ready at a moment's notice.
items.x: 즉시 대응해야 함 → vigilant(경계하는, 방심하지 않는).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The committee members held ______ views on the proposal; some praised it enthusiastically while others rejected it outright.
items.x: 찬반이 갈림 → divergent.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The author's prose is deceptively ______: its short sentences and plain words conceal layers of irony that reward careful rereading.
items.x: 짧은 문장·평이한 단어가 반어를 숨김 → 겉보기에 단순한(deceptively simple).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: Although the treaty was signed with great ______, it was quietly abandoned within a decade.
items.x: Although 대조: 성대하게 서명했지만 조용히 폐기 → fanfare.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The data were ______ with the hypothesis: the predicted increase appeared in every region studied.
items.x: 예측이 모든 지역에서 나타남 → consistent(일치하는).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The coach's ______ instructions — 'play harder' and 'be smarter' — left the players unsure what to change.
items.x: 무엇을 바꿀지 모름 → vague(모호한).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: Rather than ______ the controversy, the senator's statement only intensified it, drawing even more criticism.
items.x: Rather than ~ only intensified → 반대 의미 defusing(진정시키다).

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: In chess, beginners tend to evaluate positions by counting pieces. Masters, by contrast, often sacrifice material to gain time, space, or initiative. A position with fewer pieces can be stronger if those pieces work together. For the master, the value of a piece depends not on what it is but on _______.
o: what it can do in relation to the others
how long it has been on the board
its distance from the king alone
items.x: 기물의 가치는 다른 기물과의 관계 속 역할에 달려 있다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Some of the most effective public health campaigns never mention health at all. A program to reduce littering in Texas used the slogan 'Don't Mess with Texas,' appealing to local pride rather than environmental concern. Litter dropped dramatically. People often change behavior more readily when the message _______.
o: connects to an identity they already value
items.x: 이미 소중히 여기는 정체성과 연결될 때 행동이 쉽게 바뀐다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: When a team wins, members tend to credit their own skill; when it loses, they blame bad luck or the referees. The same pattern appears in business and politics. Because success is attributed to ability and failure to circumstance, people _______.
o: often learn less from their failures than they could
share credit equally with their rivals
judge themselves more harshly than others
items.x: 자기 고양 편향: 실패를 상황 탓으로 돌려 실패에서 덜 배운다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: The tallest trees in a dense forest are not necessarily the healthiest; they may simply have grown fast to reach light before their neighbors. In open fields, the same species grows shorter but sturdier. A tree's shape, then, tells us as much about _______ as about the tree itself.
o: the age of the soil alone
the season in which it was planted
items.x: 나무 모양은 그 나무가 겪은 경쟁 환경을 알려 준다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Libraries were once valued mainly as storehouses of books. In an age when almost any text can be found online, many libraries have reinvented themselves as places for community classes, quiet study, and access to tools people cannot afford at home. Their value has shifted from _______.
o: what they hold to what they make possible
items.x: 보관하는 것(장서) → 가능하게 하는 것(공간·기회)으로 가치 이동.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Children who are told exactly how to use a new toy tend to play with it in that one way. Children who are given the same toy without instructions often discover several functions on their own. Teaching, it seems, can sometimes _______.
o: narrow the exploration it is meant to support
make children more curious than ever
stop children from playing at all
items.x: 직접 교수가 탐색의 폭을 좁힐 수 있다.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Archaeologists studying ancient garbage heaps learn more about daily life than from palaces and temples. Monuments record what rulers wanted remembered; trash records what people actually ate, used, and threw away. For understanding ordinary lives, the most valuable evidence is often _______.
o: what no one intended to leave as a record
carved into stone by official artists
items.x: 의도치 않게 남겨진 것이 평범한 삶의 가장 귀한 증거.

items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: A new employee who asks many questions may seem less competent at first. Yet studies show that those who seek help early learn their jobs faster and make fewer serious mistakes later. Appearing uncertain for a short time can therefore be _______.
o: a reason to avoid asking questions
items.x: 초기에 모르는 티를 내는 것은 장기적 역량에 대한 투자.

items.q: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: In many languages, the words for 'left' carry negative meanings, while 'right' suggests correctness or skill. Left-handed children were once forced to write with their right hands. Such practices reveal how a simple biological variation can be loaded with cultural judgment, shaping how people are treated for reasons that have nothing to do with their abilities.
o: cultural bias attached to a natural difference
items.x: 자연적 차이(왼손잡이)에 붙은 문화적 편견.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Pilots, surgeons, and astronauts all use checklists, even for routine tasks they have performed thousands of times. Experience makes people confident, but confidence makes them skip steps. A simple list catches the small errors that experts are most likely to overlook precisely because they feel so sure of themselves.
o: Confidence as the Key to Success
items.x: 전문가도 체크리스트가 필요한 이유.

items.q:
다음 단어의 뜻으로 가장 적절한 것은?
abandon
items.x: abandon: 버리다, 포기하다 (≈ desert). 예) They had to abandon the plan when funding ran out.

items.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'abandon'?
items.x: abandon ≈ desert (버리다, 포기하다). 다른 선지: exposed, enforce, speed up, sufficient

items.q: 【 】 안 단어의 문맥상 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: They had to 【abandon】 the plan when funding ran out.
items.x: abandon = 버리다, 포기하다.

items.q:
다음 단어의 뜻으로 가장 적절한 것은?
accelerate
items.x: accelerate: 가속하다 (≈ speed up). 예) Warmer temperatures accelerate the melting of glaciers.

items.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'accelerate'?
items.x: accelerate ≈ speed up (가속하다). 다른 선지: repress, remove, believable, tough

items.q: 【 】 안 단어의 문맥상 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Warmer temperatures 【accelerate】 the melting of glaciers.
items.x: accelerate = 가속하다.

items.q:
다음 단어의 뜻으로 가장 적절한 것은?
accumulate
items.x: accumulate: 축적하다 (≈ gather). 예) Dust accumulates quickly in an unused room.

items.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'accumulate'?
items.x: accumulate ≈ gather (축적하다). 다른 선지: steady, weaken, cause, idea

items.q: 【 】 안 단어의 문맥상 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.p: Dust 【accumulates】 quickly in an unused room.
items.x: accumulate = 축적하다.

items.q:
다음 단어의 뜻으로 가장 적절한 것은?

For most of the twentieth century, basketball coaches treated the long two-point shot — taken just inside the three-point line — as a sign of a skilled scorer.
(A) A shot from just inside the line succeeds perhaps 40 percent of the time and is worth two points, so it produces about 0.8 points per attempt. A shot from a step farther back succeeds slightly less often, perhaps 36 percent of the time, but is worth three points, producing about 1.08 points per attempt.
(B) The difference looks small on a single possession, yet over a season of thousands of shots it can decide a championship. Once teams accepted this logic, the game changed rapidly.
(C) Players who could reliably hit that shot were valued, and offenses were often built around them. Then analysts began to do some simple arithmetic.

Octopuses have about 500 million neurons, a number comparable to that of a dog.
(A) Each arm can taste, touch, and even make simple decisions on its own. An arm that has been separated from the body will still reach for food and attempt to pass it toward where the mouth would be.
(B) What makes them remarkable, however, is not only how many neurons they have but where those neurons are. Roughly two-thirds are located not in the central brain but in the eight arms.
(C) This arrangement allows a level of multitasking that would be difficult for animals with centralized nervous systems. While the central brain decides on a general goal, such as 'search that crevice for crabs,' the arms work out the details independently, exploring different holes at the same time.

Before standardized time, every town set its clocks by the sun.
(A) The railways changed that. A train leaving one city and arriving in another had to follow a schedule, but whose clock should the schedule use?

items.x: hardly는 부정어 → 이중 부정 불가. 수동 완료 had been stolen.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: Although the experiment's results were ______, the researchers cautioned that a larger study was needed before drawing firm conclusions.
items.x: Although: 결과는 유망하지만 확정하려면 더 큰 연구 필요 → promising.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The critic's review was so ______ that it discussed every scene of the film in exhaustive detail.
items.x: 모든 장면을 자세히 → thorough.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: Because the bridge's design was ______, engineers from around the world came to study its unusual structure.
items.x: 전 세계가 연구하러 옴 → innovative.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.p: The diplomat's remarks were deliberately ______, allowing both sides to interpret them as support for their own positions.
items.x: 양측이 각자 유리하게 해석 → equivocal(모호한).

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.p: Electric cars produce no tailpipe emissions. ______, their overall environmental impact depends on how the electricity that charges them is generated.
items.x: 배출가스 없음 ↔ 전체 영향은 발전 방식에 달림 → However.

items.q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.p: The team tested the new material at extremely low temperatures, where it remained flexible. ______, it showed no signs of cracking after a thousand bending cycles.
items.x: 긍정 결과 추가 → Moreover.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 这次比赛他虽然输了，但他并没有______，反而更加努力地训练。
items.x: 灰心 낙심하다. 졌지만 낙심하지 않고 오히려 더 노력했다.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 经过三年的努力，他终于______了自己的梦想，成为了一名职业篮球运动员。
items.x: 实现梦想 꿈을 실현하다(고정 호응).

items.q: 빈칸에 순서대로 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 科学家们______，长期睡眠不足不仅会______人的记忆力，还可能______心脏疾病的风险。
o: 指出 / 削弱 / 增加
指示 / 减弱 / 增长
指出 / 消灭 / 增强
提出 / 削弱 / 加强
表明 / 减少 / 增多
items.x: 指出 지적하다, 削弱记忆力 기억력을 약화시키다, 增加风险 위험을 증가시키다.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 面对突如其来的困难，他表现得十分______，没有丝毫慌乱。
items.x: 从容 침착하다. 没有丝毫慌乱(조금도 당황하지 않음)과 호응.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 这个问题很复杂，我们需要______考虑，不能急于做决定。
items.x: 全面考虑 전면적으로 고려하다. 全部/完全은 부사·명사 용법이 달라 어색.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 这家公司一直______“顾客第一”的原则，因此赢得了良好的口碑。
items.x: 遵循原则 원칙을 따르다. 遵守는 규칙·법률(遵守纪律/法律)과 주로 호응.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 올바른 문장은?
items.x: 把자문은 동사 뒤 기타성분 필요(做完了). 부정사는 把 앞(没把房间打扫), 가능보어는 把자문 불가, 被자문도 결과 성분 필요(批评了一顿).

items.q: 다음 중 병구(문법적으로 틀린 문장)는?
o: 通过这次活动，使我认识到了团队合作的重要性。
这次活动让我认识到了团队合作的重要性。
通过这次活动，我认识到了团队合作的重要性。
这次活动使我认识到了团队合作的重要性。
参加这次活动以后，我认识到了团队合作的重要性。
items.x: '通过…，使…' 구조는 주어가 사라진 대표적 병구. 通过나 使 중 하나를 빼야 한다.

items.q: 다음 중 병구(문법적으로 틀린 문장)는?
o: 能否保持良好的心态，是考试取得好成绩的关键。
能否保持良好的心态，是考试能否取得好成绩的关键。
保持良好的心态，是考试取得好成绩的关键。
良好的心态是取得好成绩的关键之一。
他能不能来，现在还不确定。
items.x: 앞은 양면(能否), 뒤는 일면(取得好成绩)이라 호응 불일치(两面对一面). 뒤에도 能否를 넣거나 앞에서 빼야 한다.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 보어는?
items.p: 黑板上的字太小了，坐在后面的同学根本看______。
items.x: 글자가 작아 '똑똑히 볼 수 없다' → 看不清楚.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: ______明天下雨，比赛______会照常进行。
items.x: 即使…也… 설령 ~하더라도 ~하다 (가정 양보).

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 他______没有参加过正式的训练，______篮球却打得比谁都好。
items.x: 尽管…但… 비록 ~이지만(사실 양보). 不管/无论은 조건 무관 구문이라 의문사·선택 형식이 필요.

items.q: '了'의 위치가 가장 자연스러운 문장은?
items.x: 수량사 목적어가 있는 완료는 동사 바로 뒤에 了.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 성어는?
items.p: 学习外语不能______，要每天坚持，才能真正提高。
items.x: 三天打鱼，两天晒网 작심삼일, 꾸준하지 못함 → 매일 꾸준히 해야 한다와 대비.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 성어는?
items.p: 他的文章已经写得很好了，你再加这么多修饰，简直是______。
items.x: 画蛇添足 사족 — 이미 좋은데 불필요한 걸 더해 망침. 锦上添花는 좋은 것에 더 좋은 것을 더함(긍정).

items.q: 다음 중 성어의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 문장은?
o: 他做事总是半途而废，所以大家都很信任他。
这位老教授在学术界德高望重。
比赛前他胸有成竹，一点也不紧张。
这个计划考虑得很周到，可以说是万无一失。
听了他的解释，我才恍然大悟。
items.x: 半途而废(중도 포기)는 부정적 의미라 '그래서 다들 신뢰한다'와 모순.

items.q: '守株待兔'와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
o: 不努力而想靠运气获得成功
items.x: 守株待兔 그루터기를 지키며 토끼를 기다림 → 노력 없이 요행을 바람.

items.q: 이 글의 중심 내용으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 很多人认为，只有天才才能取得巨大的成就。然而研究表明，那些在某一领域达到顶尖水平的人，大多经过了上万小时的刻意练习。所谓刻意练习，并不是简单地重复，而是不断走出舒适区，针对自己的弱点进行有目的的训练，并及时获得反馈。天赋固然重要，但如果没有正确的练习方法，天赋也难以转化为真正的能力。
o: 正确的刻意练习是取得成就的关键
练习时间越长越好，方法不重要
舒适区有助于提高能力
items.x: 천재성보다 약점을 겨냥한 '의도적 연습'과 피드백이 성취의 핵심. ③은 '단순 반복이 아니다'와 모순.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
items.p: 熊猫看起来胖乎乎的，动作很慢，但它们其实是很好的爬树能手。小熊猫遇到危险时，常常会迅速爬到树上躲起来。此外，熊猫虽然属于食肉目动物，但它们的食物99%都是竹子。由于竹子营养较低，熊猫每天需要花十几个小时进食。
o: 熊猫每天进食时间很长
items.x: 竹子营养较低 → 每天十几个小时进食.

items.q: 밑줄 친 '这把双刃剑'이 가리키는 것으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 社交媒体让人与人之间的联系变得前所未有地方便，远在千里之外的朋友也能随时分享生活。但与此同时，不少人沉迷于刷手机，与身边的人反而越来越疏远。如何用好这把双刃剑，是每个现代人都需要思考的问题。
items.x: 편리함과 소외라는 양면성을 지닌 社交媒体를 '양날의 검'에 비유.

items.q: 작가의 태도로 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 有人说，旅行的意义在于“打卡”，去的地方越多越好。我却不这么认为。走马观花地看了一百个景点，不如静下心来，在一座城市住上一周，去菜市场买菜，和当地人聊聊天。真正的旅行，不是用眼睛看风景，而是用心去感受另一种生活。
o: 建议不要和当地人交流
items.x: 走马观花(주마간산)보다 한 도시에 머물며 현지 생활을 체험하는 여행을 주장.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 문장은?
items.p: 小王第一次参加面试，非常紧张。面试官问他为什么选择这家公司，他一时说不出话来。______，他深吸一口气，慢慢地说出了自己的想法，最后顺利通过了面试。
items.x: 말이 막힌 뒤 '잠시 후' 심호흡하고 말함 → 시간 경과 연결어.

items.q:
다음 단어를 바르게 배열한 문장은?
[ 被 / 那本书 / 借走了 / 已经 / 同学 ]
o: 那本书已经被同学借走了。
那本书被已经同学借走了。
同学已经被那本书借走了。
已经那本书被同学借走了。
那本书被同学已经借走了。
items.x: 부사(已经)는 被 앞에 위치: 주어+부사+被+행위자+동사+기타성분.

items.q:
다음 단어를 바르게 배열한 문장은?
[ 对 / 很 / 他 / 感兴趣 / 中国历史 ]
o: 他对中国历史很感兴趣。
他很对中国历史感兴趣。
他对很中国历史感兴趣。
中国历史对他很感兴趣。
他感兴趣对中国历史很。
items.x: 对+대상+很感兴趣. 정도부사 很은 感兴趣 바로 앞.

items.q:
빈칸에 공통으로 알맞은 것은?
① 他______了大家的意见，修改了计划。
② 我们应该______老师的建议。
items.x: 采纳意见/建议 의견·건의를 받아들이다. 采取는 措施/行动, 采用은 方法/技术와 호응.

items.q: 다음 중 '的/得/地' 사용이 모두 바른 문장은?
o: 他高兴地跑过来，说得很快，脸上带着灿烂的笑容。
他高兴的跑过来，说地很快，脸上带着灿烂得笑容。
他高兴得跑过来，说的很快，脸上带着灿烂地笑容。
他高兴地跑过来，说的很快，脸上带着灿烂的笑容。
他高兴的跑过来，说得很快，脸上带着灿烂地笑容。
items.x: 地: 부사어+동사(高兴地跑), 得: 동사+정도보어(说得很快), 的: 관형어+명사(灿烂的笑容).

items.q: '그는 농구를 할 줄 알 뿐만 아니라 아주 잘한다.'를 가장 자연스럽게 옮긴 것은?
o: 他不但会打篮球，而且打得很好。
他不但会打篮球，而且很好打。
他会打篮球不但，而且打得很好。
他不但打篮球会，而且打得好很。
他而且会打篮球，不但打得很好。
items.x: 不但…而且…, 정도보어 打得很好.

items.q: '이 문제는 아무리 어려워도 우리는 해결할 방법을 찾아야 한다.'를 가장 자연스럽게 옮긴 것은?
o: 这个问题不管多难，我们都要想办法解决。
这个问题即使多难，我们都要想办法解决。
这个问题虽然多难，我们也要想办法解决。
这个问题不管很难，我们都要想办法解决。
这个问题多难不管，我们都要解决办法。
items.x: 不管+의문형식(多难)+都. 即使/虽然 뒤에는 의문형식 多难을 쓰지 않는다.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 为了______环境，我们应该尽量少用一次性筷子。
items.x: 保护环境 환경을 보호하다. 保持는 状态/联系, 保存은 资料/食物, 保留는 意见/传统.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 这件事对我的______很大，让我重新思考了自己的人生。
items.x: 对…的影响很大 ~에 대한 영향이 크다. 印象은 '인상'.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 他平时很少说话，但一______篮球，就变得特别兴奋。
items.x: 一提到… 就… ~이야기만 나오면 곧.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 这项研究______了许多年，终于取得了突破性的进展。
items.x: 持续了许多年 여러 해 지속되다(상태의 지속). 继续는 중단 후 이어감, 陆续은 잇달아.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 请你把这份文件______一下，看看有没有错误。
items.x: 문서를 검사(점검)하다 → 检查. 调查는 조사, 观察는 관찰.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 他的成功并不是______，而是多年努力的结果。
items.x: 우연(偶然)이 아니라 노력의 결과.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 经过医生的治疗，他的病情已经明显______了。
items.x: 病情好转 병세가 호전되다.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 面对激烈的竞争，公司必须不断______，才能生存下去。
items.x: 기업이 끊임없이 혁신하다 → 创新. 创作는 예술 창작.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 考试的时候要______，不要因为紧张而看错题目。
items.x: 仔细 꼼꼼하다(술어로 단독 사용 가능). 详细는 내용이 상세함.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 他对自己的要求非常______，从来不允许自己犯同样的错误。
items.x: 要求严格 요구가 엄격하다. 严重은 상황이 심각, 严肃는 표정·태도가 엄숙.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 这个周末我们______去爬山，你要不要一起去？
items.x: 打算 ~할 계획이다.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 互联网的发展极大地______了人们获取信息的方式。
items.x: 改变方式 방식을 바꾸다(타동사). 变化는 주로 자동사·명사.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 这家餐厅的菜不但好吃，而且价格也很______。
items.x: 价格合理 가격이 합리적이다.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 她的演讲内容丰富，语言生动，深深地______了在场的每一位观众。
items.x: 打动观众 관중을 감동시키다(타동사). 感动도 타동사이나 '感动地'는 부사형이라 불가, 激动은 자동사.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 你别着急，问题总会有办法______的。
items.x: 解决问题 문제를 해결하다.

items.q: 빈칸에 순서대로 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 这本书______了作者童年的经历，______了那个时代普通人的生活。
items.x: 记录经历 경험을 기록, 反映生活 생활을 반영. 反应은 '반응'.

items.q: 빈칸에 순서대로 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 只有______自己的不足，才能______地进步。
items.x: 承认不足 부족함을 인정하다, 不断地进步 끊임없이 발전하다.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 天气预报说明天有雨，出门的时候别忘了______伞。
items.x: 带伞 우산을 챙기다. 戴는 모자·안경을 쓰다.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 这次失败给了我们一个深刻的______：计划再好，也要考虑到意外情况。
items.x: 深刻的教训 뼈아픈 교훈.

items.q: 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 他______努力，最后还是没有通过考试。
items.x: 尽管…还是… 비록 ~지만 그래도(사실 양보).

items.q:
빈칸에 공통으로 알맞은 것은?
① 我们要______时间，不能浪费。

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
items.p: 茶在中国已有几千年的历史。最初，人们把茶叶当作药材，后来才逐渐变成日常饮品。唐代以后，喝茶的风气在社会各个阶层普及，还出现了专门研究茶的著作《茶经》。如今，中国的茶文化已经传播到世界各地。
o: 茶最初被当作药材使用。
茶从一开始就是日常饮品。
中国茶文化没有传到国外。
items.x: 最初，人们把茶叶当作药材.

items.q: 이 글의 중심 내용으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 人们常说“失败是成功之母”。但失败本身并不会自动带来成功。如果一个人失败后不去分析原因，只是一次次地重复同样的做法，那么他得到的只会是更多的失败。真正有价值的，是从失败中总结经验、调整方法的能力。
o: 从失败中总结经验才能走向成功
重复同样的做法最有效
items.x: 실패 자체가 아니라 실패에서 교훈을 얻는 능력이 중요.

items.q: 작가가 이 글을 쓴 목적으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 很多人觉得读书没有用，因为书上的知识不能马上变成钱。但我认为，读书的意义不在于马上得到什么，而在于它慢慢改变了我们看世界的方式。一个读过很多书的人，遇到问题时会有更多的思路。
items.x: 독서의 의미는 장기적으로 세계를 보는 방식을 바꾸는 데 있다.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
items.p: 长城是世界上最长的军事防御工程，总长度超过两万公里。它并不是一次建成的，而是从春秋战国时期开始，经过多个朝代不断修建而成的。现在我们看到的长城大部分是明代修建的。
o: 长城的总长度超过两万公里。
长城修建始于春秋战国时期。
现存长城大部分修建于明代。
items.x: 并不是一次建成的 → 한 번에 완성된 것이 아니다.

items.q: 작가의 관점으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.p: 有人认为，机器翻译越来越发达，学外语已经没有必要了。我不同意这种看法。语言不仅是交流的工具，更是了解一种文化的窗口。通过机器翻译，我们也许能明白别人说了什么，却很难真正理解别人为什么这样说。
